newsitem.title: USA: NYC sees $50 mln of FY 98 savings from bond sale.
newsitem.headline: NYC sees $50 mln of FY 98 savings from bond sale.

text.p: New York City achieved about $50 million in budget relief for fiscal 1998 because of good demand and market conditions for its $739 million bond sale on Wednesday, a city official said.
The savings are $10 million more than had been planned in the fiscal 1998, which begins July 1, the city official said.
The city sold $739 million of general obligation bonds through Lehman Brothers on Wednesday. At the repricing, the yields on several maturities were lowered, reducing the city's borrowing costs.
Demand for the issue was strong, with priority orders of $542 million and another $210 million of retail orders placed, the city official said.
A total of $1.6 billion in orders were placed, he said.
"We were pleased," he said about the results of the sale.
About $196 million of the offering was insured by MBIA Insurance Corp. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
